name: SW-420 vibration sensor module
description: Vibration/shock detector: an SW-420 normally closed roller vibration switch and an LM393 comparator with a sensitivity potentiometer. The digital output DO is LOW while the module is still and goes HIGH while it vibrates (short pulses that follow the shaking); an indicator LED shows the output. Open-collector LM393 output with a 10 kOhm pull-up to VCC on the board. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: SW-420 vibration sensor module (common blue 3-pin clone board: VCC, GND, DO).
eli5: Tells your board when it gets shaken or bumped, like a tiny earthquake detector.

pins.name: VCC
pins.description: Supply, 3.3-5 V (pin 1). With a 3.3 V board connect it to 3V3, because DO is pulled up to VCC.

pins.name: DO
pins.description: Digital output (pin 3): LOW while still, HIGH while vibrating (pulled up to VCC by 10 kOhm)

buildNotes: Header order as printed: VCC, GND, DO.
On an ESP32 or Pico power VCC from 3V3: the board's pull-up takes DO to VCC, so a 5 V supply puts 5 V on the GPIO.
DO is active HIGH: 0 while still, 1 while shaking. The pulses are short, so use an interrupt (the driver's vibrated() or count()) rather than only polling.
Turn the potentiometer to set the sensitivity; if DO chatters with nothing touching the board, turn it the other way.
Mount the board firmly to the thing you want to watch; a loose module rattles and triggers by itself.

driver.code:
# SW-420 vibration sensor module, MicroPython driver.
# The SW-420 is a normally closed roller vibration switch. On the module it forms a
# divider with a 10 kOhm resistor; an LM393 comparator compares that node with the
# threshold set on the potentiometer. The LM393 output is open-collector with a
# pull-up to VCC on the board, so DO is:
#   LOW  (0) while the module is still (switch closed)
#   HIGH (1) while it vibrates (switch opens for a moment)
# Vibration pulses are short, so this driver also latches rising edges with an IRQ
# and vibrated() reports any shake since the last call.
# Power the module from 3.3 V when using a 3.3 V board: DO swings to VCC.
from machine import Pin


class SW420:
    def __init__(self, pin):
        # The board has its own pull-up on DO; no internal pull needed.
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self._hits = 0
        self.pin.irq(handler=self._edge, trigger=Pin.IRQ_RISING)

    def _edge(self, pin):
        self._hits += 1

    def raw(self):
        """Logic level on DO right now: 1 = vibrating, 0 = still."""
        return self.pin.value()

    def vibrating(self):
        """True while DO is high (the switch is open because of vibration)."""
        return self.pin.value() == 1

    def vibrated(self):
        """True if DO is high now or rose at least once since the last call."""
        hit = self._hits > 0 or self.pin.value() == 1
        self._hits = 0
        return hit

    def count(self, reset=True):
        """Number of rising edges (vibration pulses) since the last reset."""
        n = self._hits
        if reset:
            self._hits = 0
        return n

example.code:
from sw420 import SW420
import time

sensor = SW420({DO})
while True:
    print('Vibration: %s' % ('YES' if sensor.vibrated() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
